results.title: Nebius to increase prices for Nvidia GPU resources from October By Investing.com
highlights:
Investing.com -- Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1, the company said in an emailed statement, according to Bloomberg News. 

The price increases will apply to Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU resources, according to the statement. The company will also raise rates for certain CPU and memory resources.

The new pricing structure takes effect at the beginning of next month.

results.author: Matthew Broersma
highlights:
Amsterdam-based AI cloud provider Nebius said on Thursday it would raise prices for renting GPU and CPU capacity, in an indication of sustained demand for training and deploying AI models.

The move came after competitor CoreWeave said earlier in the day that it is signing new contracts at higher prices.

...

## Price hike

As of 1 October, Nebius said it would charge roughly 17 percent more for Nvidia H100 instances and 21 percent for the newer Nvidia B300, while rates for the AMD Epyc Genoa server CPU would rise by 25 percent.

Memory offerings are to rise by 41 percent, Nebius said.

The hike was Nebius’ second in three months, with pricing for B300 instances rising a cumulative 56 percent.

The company said customers reserving large-scale clusters for multiple months can receive discounts.

# Nebius (NBIS) confirms it will hike prices for on-demand CPU and GPU Services; Will raise GPU rates for Nvidia (NVDA) H100, H200, B200 and B300

Newsquawk Staff · 17 Sept 2026, 13:58 UTC

Nebius (NBIS) confirms it will hike prices for on-demand CPU and GPU Services; Will raise GPU rates for Nvidia (NVDA) H100, H200, B200 and B300.

...

Price hikes on rented GPU capacity read as a demand-outstripping-supply signal in the compute market, and historically the useful distinction is between genuine tightness and margin repair: when the whole cohort of GPU clouds and the hyperscalers are raising or holding rates in parallel it reflects scarcity of accelerators and power, while an isolated provider moving alone more often signals its own cost position. A provider explicitly able to raise rates on both current and next-generation Nvidia hardware simultaneously, including the newest parts, sits in the former category and implies demand is arriving ahead of supply even as new silicon ramps. The names listed span multiple GPU generations, which matters because rental rates on older parts normally decay once successor hardware ships; pricing power that persists across generations is the stronger tell. What tends to follow in these episodes is scrutiny of the rest of the neocloud peer set for matching moves, hyperscaler capex commentary as the forward demand proxy, and Nvidia supply commentary on whether allocation tightness is easing. Pricing power flowing to GPU landlords is generally read as corroborating, rather than substituting for, the chipmaker's order book.

results.title: Nebius Said to Raise Prices for its On-demand Compute Resources Starting October | MemoryMarket - memory prices, market analysis, industry news, research report
results.author: By: M
highlights:
According to media reports, as Nebius continues to expand its AI infrastructure globally, the company will raise prices for some of its on-demand computing resources starting October 1, marking its second round of price increases since May.

Under the new pricing plan, the price of H100 will rise from $3.85 per GPU hour to $4.50, an increase of about 17%; H200 will rise 20% from $4.50 to $5.40; B200 will rise nearly 19% from $7.15 to $8.50; and B300 will rise about 21% from $7.85 per GPU hour to $9.50. 

The changes also extend to CPU-only compute. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rates will rise 25% to $0.015 per vCPU-hour from $0.012, while Genoa memory will increase about 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour from $0.0032. 

The ultimate impact on customers' bills will therefore depend on their configurations and usage.

results.title: Nebius (NBIS) raises GPU prices up to 21% from October 1
results.author: Dennis Singleton
highlights:
Nebius (NBIS) said Thursday it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for renting selected Nvidia (NVDA) chips from October 1, its second increase in three months, Reuters reported. The stock traded as high as $232.85 in the first half hour and gave back most of that gain, closing at $217.99, up 4.1% from Wednesday's $209.37.

The increases run 17% to 21% across the Nvidia lineup. The listed CPU and memory rates rise 25% and about 41%, respectively. Nebius's own public pricing page still listed the current rates on Thursday afternoon, with no notice of the October change.

| Instance | On-demand before Oct. 1 | From Oct. 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100, per GPU-hour | $3.85 | $4.50 |
| H200, per GPU-hour | $4.50 | $5.40 |
| B200, per GPU-hour | $7.15 | $8.50 |
| B300, per GPU-hour | $7.85 | $9.50 |
| EPYC Genoa, per vCPU-hour | $0.012 | $0.015 |
| Genoa memory, per GiB-hour | $0.0032 | $0.0045 |

We confirmed the current H100, H200 and B200 rates against Nebius's published price list. The B300 rate was not listed publicly at the time, and the company quoted it through sales, so that row and the new column came from the reporting rather than from Nebius. Nebius's price list now shows the new rates, including $9.50 for the B300. The steepest increase is the cloud memory rental rate rather than any accelerator, and the Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) EPYC Genoa processor rate rises more than the GPUs as well.

Between 17% and 21% on the Nvidia accelerators, effective October 1, 2026. The H100 goes to $4.50 an hour from $3.85, the H200 to $5.40 from $4.50, the B200 to $8.50 from $7.15 and the B300 to $9.50 from $7.85. The largest increases are outside the GPUs: the AMD EPYC Genoa processor rate rises 25% per vCPU-hour and the cloud memory rental rate rises about 41% per GiB-hour. These are rental rates for cloud instances, not prices for physical memory chips.

results.title: Nebius to Raise GPU Cloud Prices About 20% from Oct. 1, Second Hike in 2026
highlights:
Nebius has announced it will raise prices for its GPU cloud services by an average of about 20% starting October 1, 2026, covering H100, H200, B200 and B300 chips. The increase is the company's second since May 2026 and was widely viewed as a sign that AI compute demand remains overheated while supply stays tight. Nebius shares rose nearly 7% in after-hours trading, while Coreweave gained about 4% and optical networking stocks including AAOI and Credo Technology advanced close to 3%.

Under the new rate card, H100 will rise from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour, up about 16.9%; H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, up 20%; B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, up about 18.9%; and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50, up about 21%. In May 2026, Nebius increased prices by an average of 29% for on-demand capacity and 51% for preemptible capacity. For B300, the cumulative increase since the pre-May price of about $6.10 per hour comes to roughly 56%.

According to market analysts, Nebius management has previously indicated that some customers have reserved capacity for the first and second quarters of 2028, with some orders involving tens of thousands of GPUs. Demand visibility now exceeds 24 months, up from about 18 months. The latest increase spans both older Hopper GPUs and the newer Blackwell lineup, suggesting demand is broad-based across AI compute types. Nvidia's strong quarterly results on September 16 reinforced expectations that AI data center buildouts will continue to drive compute supply chains.
